newsitem.title: MOROCCO: U.N. Western Sahara envoy leaves Rabat for Algiers.
newsitem.headline: U.N. Western Sahara envoy leaves Rabat for Algiers.

text.p: U.N. envoy for Western Sahara James Baker left Rabat for Algiers on Friday after talks with Moroccan leaders about a U.N. peace plan for the disputed territory, the official MAP news agency said.

"I am engaged in a mission of information...After this trip I will present a report to the U.N. secretary-general on the situation in the region," MAP quoted Baker as saying before his departure from Rabat airport.

The former U.S. Secretary of State was appointed by U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan last month to try to resolve the dispute over the former Spanish colony. Western Sahara is claimed by Morocco while the Algerian-backed Polisario Front seeks independence there.
During his 48-hour visit to Morocco Baker met King Hassan, government officials and leaders of political parties, Moroccan officials said.

A ceasefire in Western Sahara, monitored by a U.N. force, has held since 1991. But plans for a U.N. referendum on the future of the territory have been stalled since 1992 over who is eligible to vote.
Baker, touring North Africa in a Spanish military plane, will also visit Tindouf, the Polisario's rear base located in southern Algeria, and Mauritania.
